# pi-voicekit

> Voice in and voice out for the Pi coding agent: hold-to-talk dictation for **Chinese and English** with 21 offline models, plus offline text-to-speech that reads the agent's replies aloud. Local-only since 0.6.0 — no key, no endpoint, no account; the extension's own network access is the one-time model download.

## Overview

pi-voicekit adds voice input and voice output to Pi. Hold SPACE to record, release to transcribe; the audio is recognised in process by sherpa-onnx, so no audio reaches a remote speech service. 21 local models from Parakeet, Whisper, Moonshine, SenseVoice, GigaAM, Paraformer and Qwen3 come with accuracy/speed ratings and device-aware recommendations. Chinese transcripts that come back unpunctuated are punctuated offline by the in-process `punct-ct-transformer-zh-en` model (~285 MB, fetched in the background from session start, falling back to first need) — marks only, no wording changes, English not supported. TTS covers 20 offline models (Kitten, Kokoro, Piper), including auto-speak of agent responses.

Language scope: **Chinese, English and mixed Chinese–English** are supported and validated. Every other language a model happens to cover is unvalidated and on the roadmap — see the README's Language scope section.

## Privacy

No audio is uploaded to a remote speech service: capture, recognition, punctuation and synthesis all run in the Pi process, and speech playback hands a temp WAV (mode `0600`) to a local player before deleting it. Two configurations of the user's own send data off the machine, and the claim does not cover them — system audio routing (`PULSE_SERVER` / SSH audio sends playback, and capture, to another host the user chose) and `/voice-autosubmit` (the finished transcript, text rather than audio, goes to Pi and whichever model Pi is configured with). The enforceable part lives in `tests/no-cloud-egress.test.ts` — no module imports the removed WebSocket transport, names a retired vendor identifier or host, or calls `fetch` outside the two model-download modules (`model-download.ts`, `tts-local-models.ts`). That is narrower than "cannot open a socket": it binds what this repository deleted, and a future module could still build its own client.

The one outbound step is real: model files are downloaded once, on first use, from HuggingFace and GitHub releases. Upgrading from 0.5.x erases the retired credential fields from `settings.json` on the first start and reads no API key from the environment.

## Setup

1. `pi install npm:pi-voicekit` (outside Pi)
2. Open Pi, run `/voice-settings` and press ↵ on a model in the Models tab — it downloads once
3. Audio capture auto-detects: sox, ffmpeg, or arecord
4. `/voice test` reports the audio tool, the microphone and the sherpa-onnx runtime

## Commands

- `/voice-settings` — Unified settings panel (model, language, scope, device)
- `/voice-models` — Settings panel focused on the Models tab
- `/voice-setup` — Alias of `/voice-settings`
- `/voice-speak <text>` — Speak text out loud (TTS)
- `/voice-speak-models` — Browse / install TTS voice models
- `/voice-speak-info` — Diagnose TTS state
- `/voice-punctuation status` — Offline punctuation: switch, model state, last decision
- `/voice test` — Full diagnostics (audio tool, microphone, sherpa runtime)
- `/voice [on|off|dictate|stop|history]`

## Components

- `extensions/voice.ts`: Main extension — state machine, recording, settings panel handler
- `extensions/voice/config.ts`: Config loading, saving, migration, retired-key scrub
- `extensions/voice/onboarding.ts`: Model and language pickers, first-run flow
- `extensions/voice/local.ts`: Model catalog (21 models), in-process transcription
- `extensions/voice/device.ts`: Device profiling, model fitness scoring
- `extensions/voice/model-download.ts`: Download manager with resume, verification, Handy import
- `extensions/voice/sherpa-engine.ts`: sherpa-onnx bindings, recognizer lifecycle
- `extensions/voice/punctuation.ts`: Offline punctuation — marks-only splice, fail-open step
- `extensions/voice/punctuation-model.ts`: Punctuation model catalogue, digest verification and download
- `extensions/voice/settings-panel.ts`: Settings panel overlay (5 tabs)
- `extensions/voice/tts-engine.ts`: TTS engine selection and synthesis
- `extensions/voice/tts-local-models.ts`: Local TTS catalog (Kitten, Kokoro, Piper)
- `extensions/voice/tts-playback.ts`: Audio playback, WAV encoding, abort handling
- `tests/no-cloud-egress.test.ts`: The egress gate that backs the privacy claim
